x: Without John Gladwin and Mark Sinclair or John Searle and with Olly Foote not yet able to score for us it was left to the 'old firm' of Paton, Richley and North to form the spear-head of our scoring four with Alistair Horton rising to the occasion with an excellent run to close our team in.

On a very hot afternoon it was as in the Championships in March, Olly Foote all the way, albeit with a somewhat slower time and only John Bicourt in the field who was likely to give him any problems in the early stages.

Of the 36 Belgrave runners (?) entered and made it to the start on this occasion and although some fine running by Pete Gilby and Olly Foote saw us in first place after stage 2, their efforts were somewhat in vain as we slipped to 7th place due to lack of support from our absentee A team members.

Individual wins were also recorded by; Peter Gilbey- 3000 S/C- 9.29.3, Olly Foote- 10000m- 31.29, --- Derek Williams who won his first Decathlon with 5386 pts; and Paul Richley who won the Junior 3000m in 8.41.0
The race itself was blessed with fine weather and a record entry and with fine opening runs on long & short legs by Olly Foote and Mark Sinclair it looked as though we would still make it.
Following Mark Sinclair and John Gladwin are Bob Lettin(71), Leo Coy, Olly Foote, Laurie O'Hara, Mike Nouch,Eric Crutcher(70),Martin Lake,Simon Williamson(68),and Keith Sinclair(22).

John soon opened a substantial gap from Mark Sinclair and Olly Foote. Mark faded up Cambridge as second claim runner Bob Lettin came through strongly and Olly was pleased to set a P.B so soon after his Greek holiday.

Those appearing in the photographs amongst whose disguise can be seen through are:- Johnny Morris, Lionel Mann, Tootsie Gannon, Bob Bridges, Andy Paton, Ron Severn, Jackie Smiter, Geo Flanagan, Ben Cooper, Bill Laws, Olly Foote, Ross Bros, Matt Kinnane and Rin Tin Tin.
Justin Chaston was well positioned in 25th place. Our only representative in the Senior race was Olly Foote who finished 240th.

But the big surpise was Olly Foote winning the 'B' to make it a first time double in BAL Division 1 5000 m's. Another double in the shot but Abi just couldn't master the wind in the discus and settled for second.

Olly Foote ran reasonably well in the 'B' race pulling through after a slow start, but was disappointed with his time. Perhaps his previous night's revelries and arrival at the hotel in the small hours of the morning had something to do with it.
